# What Buildkite tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, which no real credential is. That
# run is forty characters and so is a whole token body — the shortest one the
# pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in lowercase where
# the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is what a case is
# about: base64url holds the letters of both, so either spelling is a body.

patterns: buildkite-token

# The prefixes, one to a kind of token. Buildkite names each of them after the
# acronym of what it calls that kind, and names no length or alphabet for any of
# them. They are one pattern rather than ten because every one of them is a
# secret that authenticates and none is published by design, so a caller has one
# decision to make about the lot.

case:     an api access token
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     an agent session token
in:       bkaa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     an agent job token
in:       bkaj_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     an unclustered agent token
in:       bkar_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     an agent token
in:       bkct_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a registry token
in:       bkpt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a portal secret
in:       bkps_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a token exchange token
in:       bktx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a portal token
in:       bkpat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a job acquisition token
in:       bkjat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

# The places a token is written.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN=bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN=«buildkite-token»

case:     a token in the authorization header a request to the api carries
in:       Authorization: Bearer bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      Authorization: Bearer «buildkite-token»

case:     a token in the json a token exchange returns
in:       {"access_token": "bktx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"}
out:      {"access_token": "«buildkite-token»"}

case:     a token in an agent configuration file
in:       token="bkct_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"
out:      token="«buildkite-token»"

case:     a token on a command line
in:       buildkite-agent start --token bkct_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      buildkite-agent start --token «buildkite-token»

# The alphabet the forty characters are written in. It is base64url — the
# letters of both cases, the digits, the hyphen and the underscore — which is
# what betterleaks admits behind seven of the ten prefixes. It is wider than
# what the two rulesets covering the API access token admit behind that one,
# lowercase and digits alone, and it is read at the wider one so that a body of
# a kind nothing states an alphabet for is not cut at its first hyphen with the
# rest of the credential left in the text. The dot belongs to neither, and it is
# what an ordinary sentence and an ordinary path are broken by.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       bkua_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef-0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a body carrying a dot
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bkua_0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef01234567

# The lengths either side of forty. Buildkite states no length for any of the
# ten kinds — what it draws is a row of asterisks, and the rulesets read those
# rows. betterleaks reads seven of the prefixes at a count exactly and the API
# access token at forty characters or at fifty-three, which is that prefix's own
# row; trufflehog reads the API access token at forty and nothing else. So one
# floor is read for all ten rather than a count apiece, at forty, the shortest
# of them: like the GitHub and npm bodies and unlike the AWS access key ID, a
# body at or above it is a token to the end of its run. The two lengths
# betterleaks carries for one prefix are why — that token's length changed, and
# a count would have left thirteen characters of every later one in the text.
#
# What the floor costs is the two cases below the first. A token cut short of
# forty keeps every random character written in front of the cut, and none of
# them is redacted — and a kind whose whole body were shorter than forty would
# be located nowhere at all, which is what the thirty-two character body pins.

case:     a body of forty characters is a token
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a body of thirty-nine characters is not
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456

case:     a whole body of thirty-two characters is not
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a token to the end of it
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345670
out:      «buildkite-token»

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts — and where the run of its alphabet carries on past
# the floor, what carries it on is redacted with the token. The hyphen and the
# underscore belong to that alphabet, so a hyphenated or underscored word
# written against a token goes with it; a space and a dot end the run.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN_bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN_«buildkite-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xbkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      x«buildkite-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567suffix
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a token
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567-suffix
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     an underscored word written against a token
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567_suffix
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567.
out:      the token is «buildkite-token».

# Two tokens written together. Every character of a prefix belongs to the
# alphabet a body is written in, the underscore closing it included, so a whole
# prefix can stand inside a body: the second token below begins five characters
# into the first, the two bodies run to the same place, and the overlapping
# spans are redacted as one. Written without that overlap the two are separate
# values, and both go.

case:     a token beginning inside the token before it
in:       bkua_bkct_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567bkct_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 bkct_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      «buildkite-token» «buildkite-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A prefix carries an underscore,
# which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding can hold
# one — and there the five characters of a prefix stand about once in a hundred
# and thirty million characters. The run from such a prefix to the end of the
# encoding is redacted whether or not Buildkite issued it. That is the answer
# rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a token's format exactly and
# nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing these would spare a real
# token written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that was
# already opaque to a reader.
#
# Every body written in this file is forty hexadecimal characters, which is a
# SHA-1's shape exactly, so each of the cases above is also a digest behind a
# prefix and is redacted for the same reason.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzbkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«buildkite-token»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzbkua_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567zzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«buildkite-token»

# And the readable text the floor leaves. The alphabet holds the underscore and
# the hyphen, so snake_case and kebab-case run through it unbroken: a name
# opening with one of these prefixes and carrying forty more characters of the
# alphabet is a token's format exactly and is redacted. Raising the floor is
# what would rule it out, and forty is the shortest body any source attests, so
# a higher one would turn a real API access token away. A shorter name is left
# alone, and a dotted one is broken by the dot long before forty characters of
# it have been read.

case:     a snake case name long enough to reach the floor
in:       bkct_agent_token_for_the_production_cluster_east
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a kebab case name long enough to reach the floor
in:       bkct_agent-token-for-the-production-cluster-east
out:      «buildkite-token»

case:     a shorter name behind the prefix
in:       bkct_agent_token_for_production
out:      bkct_agent_token_for_production

case:     a dotted name behind the prefix
in:       bkct_agent.token.for.the.production.cluster.east
out:      bkct_agent.token.for.the.production.cluster.east

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read in
# the case Buildkite writes it and with the separator it closes on. The two
# after them are the acronym: one Buildkite names no token with, and one of its
# own with a character written into it, which moves the separator off both
# depths a kind may close at. Then the anchor and the run — a run of the right
# length with no prefix in front of it, and a body a space has broken — and a
# digest and a sentence, which hold no underscore where a prefix wants one and
# so hold no position to be found at however long they run.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       BKUA_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      BKUA_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       bkua-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bkua-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the opening with no acronym behind it
in:       bk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an acronym Buildkite names no token with
in:       bkzz_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bkzz_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a character written into an acronym
in:       bkuaa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bkuaa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       bkua_0123456789abcdef 0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      bkua_0123456789abcdef 0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And a Buildkite secret this pattern has nothing to say about. The value in a
# pipeline trigger's URL carries a bk prefix of its own, bktr_, which Buildkite
# neither calls a token nor lists among them — so reading it would have this
# pattern locate more than its name covers. A caller who wants it redacted has
# MustRegexp.

case:     the value in a pipeline trigger url
in:       https://webhook.buildkite.com/deliver/bktr_0123456789ab
out:      https://webhook.buildkite.com/deliver/bktr_0123456789ab
